ἀδελφός, -οῦ, ὁ 
(ἀ- copul., δελφύς, womb), 
in cl., a brother, born of the same parent or parents. [In LXX (Hort, Ja., 102f.), for אָח ;] 
__1. lit. of a brother (Gen.4.2, al.). 
__2. Of a neighbour (Lev.19.17). 
__3. Of a member of the same nation (Exo.2.14, Deu.15.3). In NT in each of these senses (1. Mat.1.2, al.; 2. Mat.7.3 3. Rom.9.3) and also, 
__4. of a fellow-Christian: 1Co.1.1, Act.9.30. This usage finds illustration in π., where ἀ. is used of members of a pagan religious community (M, Th., I, 1:4; MM, VGT, see word). The ἀδελφοὶ τ. Κυρίου (Mat.12.46-49; 13.55; 28.10, Mrk.3.31-34, Luk.8.19-21, Jhn.2.12; 7.3, 5, 10; 20.17, Act.1.14, 1Co.9.5) may have been sons of Joseph and Mary…

brother
